# InfiniteQuery API

URL: /reference/infinite-queries/
Type: reference

`InfiniteQuery<T, P>` paginates with caller-provided param callbacks, accumulating an `InfiniteData<T, P>`. This page lists every signature; the [pagination guide](/guides/infinite-queries/) shows the flow.

## `InfiniteQuery<T, P>` builder

| Builder                                       | Default | Description                                                    |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `InfiniteQuery::new(key, fetch_fn, initial_page_param)` | — | Key, closure `Fn(P) -> Future<Result<T, E>>`, start param |
| `.get_next_page_param(f)`                      | none    | `Fn(&T, &[T]) -> Option<P>` from the last page; `None` ends forward paging |
| `.get_previous_page_param(f)`                  | none    | `Fn(&T, &[T]) -> Option<P>` from the first page; enables backward paging |
| `.max_pages(usize)`                            | unbounded | Window size; append evicts front, prepend evicts back        |
| `.stale_time(Duration)` and friends            | —       | Standard query options apply                                    |

## `InfiniteData<T, P>`

| Member                            | Description                                       |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `.pages` / `.page_params`          | Pages in fetch order, params alongside            |
| `.new()` / `::with_first_page(page, param)` | Empty, or seeded                        |
| `.push_page(page, param)`          | Append one page                                   |
| `.page_count() -> usize`           | Current window size                               |
| `.first_page() -> Option<&T>` / `.last_page() -> Option<&T>` | Window ends              |

## Running

| Call                                            | Returns                              |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `spawn_infinite_query(&client, &query)`          | `SpawnedTask<QueryState<InfiniteData<T, P>>>` |
| `InfiniteQueryObserver`                          | Reactive observer for bindings        |
| `client.get_infinite_data::<T, P>(&key)`         | Cached pages                          |
| `client.set_infinite_data(&key, data, opts)`     | Replace pages                         |
| `client.append_infinite_page(&key, page, param, opts)` | Append with windowing           |
| `client.prepend_infinite_page(&key, page, param, opts)` | Prepend with windowing          |

The page loop runs on the client's runtime with a capacity-1 request slot: a request issued while one is in flight replaces the queued one (drop-newest), matching upstream semantics.

## Observer controls

| Method                                      | Description                                       |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `fetch_next_page()`                          | Append the next page                              |
| `fetch_previous_page()`                      | Prepend the previous page                         |
| `fetch_next_page_with(cancel_refetch, throw_on_error)` | Explicit TanStack flags                 |
| `fetch_previous_page_with(cancel_refetch, throw_on_error)` | Explicit TanStack flags              |
| `has_next_page() -> bool`                    | A next param exists                               |
| `has_previous_page() -> bool`                | A previous param exists                           |
| `is_fetching() -> bool`                      | Any page fetch in flight                          |
| `is_fetching_next_page() -> bool`            | Forward fetch in flight (`FetchDirection::Forward`) |
| `is_fetching_previous_page() -> bool`        | Backward fetch in flight (`FetchDirection::Backward`) |
| `observer() -> Arc<InfiniteQueryObserver<T, P>>` | The underlying observer (binding handle)      |

## Dehydration

Infinite queries dehydrate with `query_type = QUERY_TYPE_INFINITE` and rehydrate into the same pages/params shape — see [persistence and hydration](/reference/persistence-and-hydration/).

## Example: windowed two-way pager

<Code lang="rust" code={`use rs_query::{InfiniteQuery, QueryKey};

let query = InfiniteQuery::<Vec<Msg>, i64>::new(
    QueryKey::new("messages"),
    |cursor: i64| async move { fetch_messages_around(cursor).await },
    0,
)
.get_next_page_param(|last, _| last.last().map(|m| m.id))
.get_previous_page_param(|first, _| first.first().map(|m| m.id))
.max_pages(10);`} />

## Next steps

<LinkCard title="Guide: Infinite queries" href="/guides/infinite-queries/" description="The pagination walkthrough." />
<LinkCard title="Reference: Observers" href="/reference/observers/" description="The flag surface shared with plain queries." />

# QueryKey and Filters

URL: /reference/keys-and-filters/
Type: reference

Keys identify; filters select. `QueryKey` builds the hierarchical identity of a query, and the filter structs describe *which* queries a bulk operation touches. Both are plain data with builder methods.

## `QueryKey`

| Member                                        | Description                                            |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `QueryKey::new(segment)`                       | Start a key with a root segment                         |
| `.with(label, value) -> Self`                  | Append a labelled segment — `with("id", 42)`            |
| `.segment(name) -> Self`                       | Append a plain segment                                  |
| `QueryKey::from_segments(iter)`                | Build from an iterator of strings                       |
| `.cache_key() -> &str`                          | Stable hashed identity used by the cache and devtools   |
| `.segments() -> &[String]`                      | The raw segments                                        |
| `.starts_with(&prefix) -> bool`                 | Prefix match — the rule behind key filters              |

## `QueryFilters`

| Builder                        | Default | Description                                          |
| ------------------------------ | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `QueryFilters::all()`           | —       | Match everything                                     |
| `QueryFilters::with_key(key)`   | —       | Match keys with this prefix                          |
| `.exact()`                      | prefix  | Exact key match only                                 |
| `.active()` / `.inactive()`      | both    | At least one active observer / none                  |
| `.stale()`                      | any     | Stale by flag or by `stale_time`                     |
| `.status(status)`               | any     | `QueryStatus::Pending/Error/Success`                 |
| `.fetch_status(f)`              | any     | `FetchStatus::Idle/Fetching/Paused`                  |
| `.predicate(p)`                 | —       | `Arc<dyn Fn(&QuerySnapshot) -> bool>`                |
| `.is_stale_only() -> bool`      | —       | Whether this filter reduces to "stale"               |

## `InvalidateQueryFilters` and `RefetchQueryFilters`

<Code lang="rust" code={`InvalidateQueryFilters::new()
    .filters(QueryFilters::with_key(QueryKey::new("users")))
    .refetch_type(RefetchType::Active)`} />

| Struct                  | Builders                                       | Used by                    |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| `InvalidateQueryFilters` | `.filters(f)`, `.refetch_type(t)`              | `invalidate_queries_filtered` |
| `RefetchQueryFilters`    | `.filters(f)`, `.cancel_refetch(bool)`, `.throw_on_error(bool)` | `refetch_queries` |

`RefetchType`: `All` (refetch every match), `Active` (refetch active, mark inactive stale — the TanStack invalidation default), `Inactive` (the inverse), `None` (mark stale, refetch nothing).

## Snapshots

Filters and predicates see immutable snapshots, not live queries:

| Field (`QuerySnapshot`) | Type          | Meaning                                  |
| ----------------------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `key`                    | `QueryKey`    | The query's key                          |
| `is_active`              | `bool`        | Subscribed observer exists and is enabled |
| `is_stale`               | `bool`        | Stale by flag or `stale_time`            |
| `fetch_status`           | `FetchStatus` | Aggregate fetch status                   |
| `status`                 | `QueryStatus` | Aggregate status                         |
| `has_data`               | `bool`        | Cached data exists                       |

`QuerySnapshot::new(key, is_active, is_stale, fetch_status, status, has_data)` builds one for tests. `QueryType::All/Active/Inactive` tags filter categories.

## Mutation-side mirrors

| Item                        | Fields / builders                                                     |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `MutationSnapshot`           | `mutation_key: Option<QueryKey>`, `status: MutationStatus`, `is_paused: bool` |
| `MutationFilters`            | `all()`, `with_key(k)`, `.exact()`, `.status(s)`, `.paused()`, `.predicate(p)` |
| `match_query(snapshot, filters)`      | The matcher the client uses for queries     |
| `match_mutation(snapshot, filters)`   | The matcher for mutations                   |

## Example: preview then act

<Code lang="rust" code={`use std::sync::Arc;
use rs_query::{QueryFilters, QueryKey};

let stale_users = QueryFilters::with_key(QueryKey::new("users"))
    .stale()
    .predicate(Arc::new(|snap| snap.fetch_status == rs_query::FetchStatus::Idle));

let matched = client.query_snapshots(&stale_users);
println!("would reset {} queries", matched.len());
let _ = client.reset_queries(&stale_users);`} />

## Next steps

<LinkCard title="Guide: Working with keys and filters" href="/guides/keys-and-filters/" description="Task-oriented patterns for the same API." />
<LinkCard title="Reference: QueryClient" href="/reference/client/" description="The bulk operations these filters drive." />

# Mutation API

URL: /reference/mutations/
Type: reference

`Mutation<T, P>` runs an async write with lifecycle hooks, retry control, and scope serialization. The `MutationCache` tracks entries and broadcasts events. This page is the signature reference; the [mutation guide](/guides/mutations/) shows the patterns.

## `Mutation<T, P>` builder

| Builder                             | Default        | Description                                            |
| ----------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Mutation::new(mutate_fn)`           | —              | `Fn(P) -> impl Future<Output = Result<T, E>>`          |
| `.mutation_key(QueryKey)`            | none           | Identity for filters and the cache                     |
| `.scope(MutationScope { id })`       | none           | Mutations sharing a scope id run one at a time          |
| `.on_mutate(f)`                      | none           | Runs first; may return a rollback closure               |
| `.on_success(f)` / `.on_error(f)`    | none           | Settle hooks; receive `&QueryClient` and data/error     |
| `.on_settled(f)`                     | none           | Runs after success or error                             |
| `.retry(u32)`                        | `0`            | Mutation retry budget                                   |
| `.retry_delay(Duration)`             | `BASE_RETRY_DELAY` | Fixed retry delay                                   |
| `.network_mode(NetworkMode)`         | `Online`       | `OfflineFirst` runs attempt one offline, then pauses    |
| `.invalidates_key(key)` / `.invalidates(Vec<QueryKey>)` | none | Refetch these keys on success |

## `MutateOptions<T, P>`

Per-call callbacks passed at mutation time. They fire **last**, after the cache-level and mutation-level hooks:

| Builder            | Fires                                   |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------- |
| `.on_success(f)`    | After the mutation succeeds             |
| `.on_error(f)`      | After the mutation fails                |
| `.on_settled(f)`    | After success or error                  |

Side-effect order, TanStack-exact: cache `on_mutate` → options `on_mutate` → pending dispatch → mutation function → cache/options `on_success`/`on_error` → per-call `MutateOptions` → `on_settled` chain.

## Execution entry points

| Call                                                  | Returns                        | Notes                                |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------ |
| `execute_mutation(&client, &mutation, params)`         | `MutationState<T>` (await)     | No per-call callbacks                |
| `execute_mutation_full(&client, &mutation, params, opts)` | `MutationState<T>` (await) | With `MutateOptions`                 |
| `spawn_mutation(&client, &mutation, params)`           | `SpawnedTask<MutationState<T>>`| Awaitable, abortable, drop-cancels   |

## `MutationState<T>` and `MutationStatus`

| `MutationState` variant | Meaning                       |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| `Idle`                   | Not executed, or reset        |
| `Loading`                | Executing                     |
| `Success(T)`             | Last execution succeeded      |
| `Error(QueryError)`      | Last execution failed         |

`MutationStatus` — the aggregate mirror — maps to `Idle`/`Pending`/`Success`/`Error` with TanStack-compatible `as_str()` names. Predicates: `is_idle()`, `is_loading()`, `is_success()`, `is_error()`, `data()`, `error()`, `status()`.

## `MutationCache`

| Member                                     | Description                                       |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `MutationCache::new()` / `::with_config(cfg)` | Plain, or with cache-level callbacks            |
| `.subscribe() -> bus::Receiver<MutationCacheEvent>` | Event stream                              |
| `.add(entry) -> u64` / `.build(entry) -> u64` | Insert an entry; `build` also snapshots          |
| `.update(id, apply) -> bool`                | Mutate an entry in place                          |
| `.remove(id) -> bool` / `.clear()`          | Evict one / all                                   |
| `.get(id) -> Option<MutationCacheEntry>` / `.get_all()` | Read entries                         |
| `.find(&filters)` / `.find_all(&filters)`   | Filter-aware lookup                               |
| `.len()` / `.is_empty()`                    | Size                                              |
| `.can_run(scope)` / `.mark_running(scope)` / `.mark_finished(scope)` | Scope serialization primitives |
| `.subscribe_scope(scope)`                   | Watcher for one scope's queue                     |
| `.resume_paused_mutations()`                | Resume offline-paused entries                     |

`MutationCacheConfig` holds optional cache-level callbacks: `on_mutate`, `on_success`, `on_error`, `on_settled` — each `Arc<dyn Fn(&QueryClient, ...)>`, invoked for every mutation in the cache.

`MutationCacheEvent`: `Added(u64)`, `Removed(u64)`, `Updated(u64)`, `ScopeResumed(String)`, `Cleared`.

`MutationCacheEntry` exposes `id`, `mutation_key`, `scope`, `status`, `is_paused`, `submitted_at_ms`, `has_result`, `error`, `has_context`, and `snapshot()` → `MutationSnapshot`.

`MutationScope { id: String }` — equal ids serialize.

## `MutationObserver`

`MutationObserver<T, P>` subscribes one mutation's state changes for framework bindings; `use_mutation` builds on it. It pairs with `use_is_mutating`/`use_mutating_count` for aggregate dashboards.

## Example: scoped saves with cache callbacks

<Code lang="rust" code={`use std::sync::Arc;
use rs_query::{MutationCache, MutationCacheConfig, MutationScope};

let cache = MutationCache::with_config(MutationCacheConfig {
    on_error: Some(Arc::new(|_client, error| log(&error.to_string()))),
    ..MutationCacheConfig::default()
});`} />

## Next steps

<LinkCard title="Guide: Mutations and optimistic updates" href="/guides/mutations/" description="The optimistic-update walkthrough." />
<LinkCard title="Reference: Errors and cancellation" href="/reference/errors-and-cancellation/" description="QueryError, the type behind every failure." />

# Observers and Result Flags

URL: /reference/observers/
Type: reference

Observers turn cache state into render-ready results. `QueryObserver<T>` watches one query and derives TanStack's full boolean/timestamp flag block; `QueriesObserver<T>` watches many and supports `combine`. Framework bindings build on both.

## `QueryObserver<T>`

Constructed over a client, a key, and options; it subscribes to the cache and re-derives its result on every relevant update.

<Code lang="rust" code={`use std::sync::Arc;
use rs_query::{QueryObserver, QueryOptions};

let observer = QueryObserver::new(client.clone(), key.clone(), QueryOptions::default());`} />

The observer exposes the current `QueryState<T>`, the `QueryResultFlags` block, and `QueryStateUpdate` notifications on its bus receiver.

## `QueryResultFlags`

TanStack `QueryObserverResult` parity — every field, its type, and meaning:

| Field                 | Type              | Meaning                                                |
| --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `data_updated_at`      | `Option<Instant>` | Last successful data write (observer-local)            |
| `error_updated_at`     | `Option<Instant>` | Last error                                             |
| `error_update_count`   | `u32`             | Errors this observer has observed                      |
| `failure_count`        | `u32`             | Failed attempts for the current fetch (resets on fetch/success) |
| `failure_reason`       | `Option<QueryError>` | Last failure reason                                 |
| `is_fetched`           | `bool`            | Any fetch completed (success or error)                 |
| `is_fetched_after_mount` | `bool`          | A fetch completed after this observer was constructed  |
| `is_loading_error`     | `bool`            | Last fetch failed with no data available               |
| `is_refetch_error`     | `bool`            | Last fetch failed but data is available                |
| `is_placeholder_data`  | `bool`            | Placeholder is currently shown                         |
| `is_paused`            | `bool`            | Network mode forbids starting a fetch now              |
| `is_enabled`           | `bool`            | Options resolve to enabled                             |

## `QueryStateUpdate` and `QueryStateVariant`

Subscriptions deliver `QueryStateUpdate { key: String, state_variant: QueryStateVariant }` — the cache key plus the kind of transition. `QueryStateVariant` covers the transition classes (success, error, and the loading family) so consumers can filter without deserializing full states.

## `QueriesObserver<T>`

Coordinates a list of query specs, with TanStack's `combine`:

| Method                                  | Description                                            |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `QueriesObserver::new(&client, specs: Vec<Query<T>>)` | Build over specs                          |
| `.set_specs(specs) -> Vec<SpawnedTask<QueryState<T>>>` | Swap specs; returns the new tasks         |
| `.run_all() -> Vec<SpawnedTask<...>>`    | Fetch every spec                                       |
| `.refresh(idx) -> Option<SpawnedTask<...>>` | Refetch one index                                   |
| `.sync()`                                | Reconcile observer state with the specs                |
| `.results() -> &[QueryState<T>]`         | Current states                                         |
| `.combine(f) -> R`                       | Fold all states into one derived value                 |
| `.len()` / `.is_empty()` / `.specs()`    | Size and spec access                                   |

`combine` is what powers `use_queries`: derive a `bool` like "all loaded", a tuple of rows, or any reduction — the signal updates when any input changes.

## `MutationObserver<T, P>`

The mutation-side observer: subscribes one mutation's `MutationState<T>` transitions for `use_mutation`. Pair it with `MutationFilters` through the cache when you need aggregate counts instead.

## Example: combine for a composite view

<Code lang="rust" code={`use rs_query::QueriesObserver;

let combined = observer.combine(|states| {
    let loaded = states.iter().filter(|s| s.is_success()).count();
    (loaded, states.len())
});`} />

## Next steps

<LinkCard title="Reference: Framework hooks" href="/reference/hooks/" description="The bindings that consume these observers." />
<LinkCard title="Reference: Query and QueryState" href="/reference/query/" description="The states the flags are derived from." />

# Persistence and Hydration API

URL: /reference/persistence-and-hydration/
Type: reference

Three layers move cache state across time and process boundaries: `dehydrate`/`hydrate` produce and consume snapshots, the query persister stores individual results, and the client persister round-trips whole clients. Broadcast sync keeps live clients in step. This page is the signature reference.

## Hydration types

| Type / function                              | Description                                            |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `dehydrate_state(&client, DehydrateOptions) -> DehydratedState` | Snapshot qualifying queries and mutations |
| `hydrate_with_options(&client, &state, HydrateOptions)`         | Write a snapshot into a client            |
| `DehydratedState`                             | `dehydrated_at_ms`, `queries: Vec<DehydratedQuery>`, `mutations: Vec<DehydratedMutation>` |
| `DehydratedQuery`                             | `query_hash`, `query_key: Vec<String>`, `data_json`, `error_json`, `fetched_at_ms`, `is_stale`, `stale_time_ms`, `gc_time_ms`, `meta`, `query_type` |
| `DehydratedMutation`                          | `mutation_key`, `data_updated_at_ms`, `is_paused`      |
| `QUERY_TYPE_QUERY` / `QUERY_TYPE_INFINITE`     | `query_type` tags — infinite queries round-trip their pages |

### `DehydrateOptions`

| Option                      | Default   | Description                                        |
| --------------------------- | --------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `should_dehydrate_query(f)`  | everything | `Arc<dyn Fn(&DehydratedQuery) -> bool>`            |
| `should_dehydrate_mutation(f)` | everything | `Arc<dyn Fn(&DehydratedMutation) -> bool>`        |
| `should_redact_errors`       | `true`     | Replace errors with `QueryError::Redacted` (`"redacted"`) |
| `serialize_data(f)`          | JSON default | Custom `Arc` serializer for `data_json`          |

### `HydrateOptions`

| Option              | Default | Description                                              |
| ------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `should_overwrite`   | `false` | Overwrite locally *newer* cached data (the newer-data guard) |

Hydration resets each restored query's `fetchStatus` to idle and applies the client's default options.

## Per-query persister

| Item                                        | Description                                            |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `QueryPersister::new(QueryPersisterOptions)` | The `experimental_createQueryPersister` port           |
| `QueryPersisterOptions::new(storage)`        | Storage backend plus the knobs below                   |
| `.with_max_age(Duration)`                    | Entries older than this read as absent                 |
| `.with_buster(String)`                       | Version stamp; mismatch reads as absent                |
| `.with_prefix(String)`                       | Namespace keys in the store                            |
| `QueryStorage`                                | Trait: async key/value over `PersistedQuery` records   |
| `InMemoryQueryStorage`                        | Built-in backend                                       |
| `PersistedQuery` / `PersistedQueryState`      | Stored record and its state                            |
| `serialize_persisted_query` / `deserialize_persisted_query` | JSON helpers behind the `serde` feature  |

Restore is selective (touched-by-observer queries only) and a GC pass evicts expired records.

## Client persister

| Item                                            | Description                                        |
| ----------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `persist_query_client(&client, &options) -> PersistQueryClientHandle` | Restore + throttled save loop |
| `persist_query_client_restore(&client, ...)`     | Restore step alone                                 |
| `persist_query_client_save(&client, ...)`        | Save step alone                                    |
| `PersistQueryClientOptions::new(persister)`       | `.with_max_age(...)` (default 24 h), `.with_buster(...)` |
| `ClientPersister`                                 | Trait for the whole-client store                   |
| `InMemoryClientPersister`                         | Built-in backend                                   |
| `PersistedClient`                                 | `timestamp_ms`, `buster`, `client_state: DehydratedState` |
| `PersistQueryClientHandle`                        | `unsubscribe`, save task handle                    |
| `persist_with_retry(&client, ..., strategy)`      | Retry failing restores                             |
| `remove_oldest_query`                             | Strategy: evict the oldest query each round        |
| `MAX_RESTORE_RETRIES`                             | Retry ceiling for `persist_with_retry`             |

## Broadcast sync

| Item                                        | Description                                            |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `broadcast_query_client(&client, channel) -> BroadcastHandle` | Live sync across client instances    |
| `broadcast_query_client_with_options(&client, channel, opts)` | Option-object form                   |
| `BroadcastQueryClientOptions::new().with_channel(s)` | Channel configuration                          |
| `BroadcastHandle`                             | `unsubscribe()`, `into_task()`, `is_applying_remote()` |
| `publish_state(&client, channel)`             | One-shot snapshot push                                 |

A re-entrancy guard guarantees remote updates are applied but never re-broadcast — no echo loops between tabs.

## Next steps

<LinkCard title="Guide: Persisting the cache" href="/guides/persistence/" description="Task-oriented walkthrough of these layers." />
<LinkCard title="Guide: Hydration and dehydration" href="/guides/hydration/" description="Server-to-client round trips." />

# QueryOptions

URL: /reference/query-options/
Type: reference

`QueryOptions` is the flat option surface that mirrors TanStack v5's per-query options, field for field. Every builder method consumes and returns `Self`. Options attach to a `Query` via builder methods, flow through `QueryClient::set_default_options`, and ride on `set_query_data` calls.

## Fields and builders

| Option (builder)                                        | Type             | Default                | Description                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `stale_time` (`.stale_time(Duration)`)                   | `Duration`        | `0`                    | Data older than this is stale                             |
| `stale_time_static` (`.stale_time_static()`)             | `bool`            | `false`                | Never stale — `staleTime: 'static'`                       |
| `gc_time` (`.gc_time(Duration)`)                         | `Duration`        | `DEFAULT_GC_TIME` (5 min) | Idle eviction window                                   |
| `retry` (`.retry(RetryConfig)`)                          | `RetryConfig`     | see below              | Attempt count and backoff                                 |
| `enabled` (`.enabled(bool)`)                             | `bool`            | `true`                 | Master gate for automatic fetches                         |
| `enabled_fn` (`.enabled_fn(f)`)                          | `Option<Arc<dyn Fn() -> bool>>` | none     | Dynamic gate evaluated at fetch decision time             |
| `refetch_on_window_focus` (`.refetch_on_window_focus(t)`) | `RefetchTrigger` | `Enabled`             | Focus refetch policy                                      |
| `refetch_on_reconnect` (`.refetch_on_reconnect(t)`)      | `RefetchTrigger`  | `Enabled`              | Reconnect refetch policy                                  |
| `refetch_on_mount` (`.refetch_on_mount(t)`)              | `RefetchTrigger`  | `Enabled`              | Mount refetch policy                                      |
| `refetch_interval` (`.refetch_interval(d)`)              | `Duration`        | none                   | Poll while observers exist                                |
| `refetch_interval_in_background` (`.refetch_interval_in_background(b)`) | `bool` | `false`      | Keep polling with no active observer                      |
| `structural_sharing` (`.structural_sharing(bool)`)       | `bool`            | `true`                 | `Arc` reuse when new data `PartialEq`-compares equal       |
| `network_mode` (`.network_mode(mode)`)                   | `NetworkMode`     | `Online`               | Offline start/retry semantics                             |
| `retry_on_mount` (`.retry_on_mount(bool)`)               | `bool`            | `true`                 | Retry a failed query on the next mount                     |
| `throw_on_error` (`.throw_on_error(bool)`)               | `bool`            | `false`                | Surface errors to the caller instead of the error state    |
| `notify_on_change_props` (`.notify_on_change_props(v)`)  | `Option<Vec<String>>` | none              | Restrict change notifications to the named properties      |
| `meta` (`.meta(key, value)`)                             | `BTreeMap<String, String>` | empty        | Free-form metadata; travels with dehydration               |

`is_enabled()` resolves the effective gate: `enabled && (enabled_fn.is_none() || enabled_fn())`.

## `RetryConfig`

| Builder                              | Default              | Description                                    |
| ------------------------------------ | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `RetryConfig::new(max_retries)`       | —                    | Attempt budget                                 |
| `.base_delay(Duration)`               | `BASE_RETRY_DELAY` (1 s) | Delay before the first retry               |
| `.max_delay(Duration)`                | `MAX_RETRY_DELAY` (30 s) | Backoff ceiling                            |
| `.exponential_backoff(bool)`          | `true`               | Double each attempt when enabled               |
| `.delay_for_attempt(n) -> Duration`   | —                    | `min(1000 ms · 2ⁿ, 30 s)` when backoff is on   |
| `.should_retry(n) -> bool`            | —                    | Whether attempt `n` is within budget           |

The retryer module adds the decision layer: `RetryDecision::Never`, `RetryDecision::Count(n)`, `RetryDecision::Always`, and a closure decision, applied by `Retryer` with `retry_delay` as the math. Failure counts and reasons surface on observer results as `failure_count`/`failure_reason`.

## `PlaceholderData<T>`

| Constructor          | Behavior                                            |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `PlaceholderData::value(data)` | Always show this data while loading        |
| `PlaceholderData::function(f)` | Derive from the previous query's data       |
| `.keep_previous()`            | Reuse the previous key's data (`keepPreviousData`) |
| `.resolve(previous) -> T`      | Evaluate against `Option<&T>` at read time   |

## `RefetchTrigger`

| Variant    | Refetches…                        |
| ---------- | --------------------------------- |
| `Enabled`   | Only when the data is stale (default) |
| `Always`    | Regardless of staleness           |
| `Disabled`  | Never, from this trigger          |

`.allows_refetch(is_stale)` encodes the rule; `.is_enabled()` distinguishes `Disabled` from the rest.

## Constants

| Constant            | Value     | Role                       |
| ------------------- | --------- | -------------------------- |
| `BASE_RETRY_DELAY`   | `1 s`     | First retry delay          |
| `MAX_RETRY_DELAY`    | `30 s`    | Backoff ceiling            |
| `DEFAULT_GC_TIME`    | `5 min`   | Default cache eviction window |

## Example

<Code lang="rust" code={`use std::time::Duration;
use rs_query::{NetworkMode, QueryOptions, RefetchTrigger, RetryConfig};

let options = QueryOptions::default()
    .stale_time(Duration::from_secs(60))
    .gc_time(Duration::from_secs(600))
    .retry(RetryConfig::new(3).max_delay(Duration::from_secs(10)))
    .refetch_on_reconnect(RefetchTrigger::Always)
    .network_mode(NetworkMode::OfflineFirst)
    .meta("source", "api");`} />

<LinkCard title="Reference: QueryClient" href="/reference/client/" description="Where defaults and options meet the cache." />
<LinkCard title="Reference: Errors and cancellation" href="/reference/errors-and-cancellation/" description="What happens when every retry fails." />

# Query and QueryState

URL: /reference/query/
Type: reference

`Query<T>` describes one cacheable fetch: a `QueryKey`, an async fetch closure, and options. Running it produces a `QueryState<T>` — an exhaustive enum of cache situations. This page documents the builder, the state machine, and the three status enums every observer and snapshot uses.

## `Query<T>` builder

| Builder                            | Default            | Description                                                  |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Query::new(key, fetch_fn)`         | —                  | Key plus async closure returning `Result<T, E>`               |
| `.stale_time(Duration)`             | `0` (immediately stale) | Freshness window after a successful fetch               |
| `.stale_time_static()`              | —                  | Data never goes stale (`staleTime: 'static'`)                 |
| `.gc_time(Duration)`                | `DEFAULT_GC_TIME`  | Idle eviction window                                          |
| `.retry(RetryConfig)`               | `RetryConfig::default()` | Attempt count and backoff                               |
| `.initial_data(data)`               | none               | Seed the cache as if fetched — marked with a timestamp of zero |
| `.placeholder_data(PlaceholderData)` | none              | Show data while loading; never persisted to the cache         |
| `.select(f)`                        | identity           | Transform the data for observers without changing the cache    |
| `.enabled(bool)` / `.enabled_fn(f)` | enabled            | Gate automatic fetches                                         |
| `.network_mode(mode)`               | `NetworkMode::Online` | Offline start/retry semantics                               |
| `.structural_sharing(bool)`         | enabled            | `Arc` reuse when new data compares equal to old                |

`initial_data` and `placeholder_data` differ in one sentence: initial data **is** cache data (with an old timestamp, so it is stale), placeholder data is **display-only** during loading and never enters the cache. `PlaceholderData` builds with `.value(data)`, `.function(f)` (derive from the previous query's data), or `.keep_previous()`.

## `QueryState<T>`

| Variant                       | Meaning                                                        |
| ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Idle`                         | Never run, or reset                                            |
| `Loading`                      | First fetch in flight, nothing to show                         |
| `LoadingWithPlaceholder(T)`    | First fetch in flight over placeholder data                    |
| `Refetching(T)`                | Background refetch in flight over existing data                |
| `Success(T)`                   | Fresh data available                                           |
| `Stale(T)`                     | Data older than `stale_time`                                   |
| `Error { error, stale_data }`  | Last fetch failed; previously cached data may still render     |

Key methods: `data() -> Option<&T>`, `data_mut()`, `data_cloned()`, `map(f)`, `unwrap()`, `has_data()`, `status()`, `fetch_status()`, plus the predicates `is_idle()`, `is_loading()`, `is_refetching()`, `is_success()`, `is_stale()`, `is_error()`, and `error() -> Option<&QueryError>`.

## Status enums

### `QueryStatus` — is there data?

| Variant   | `as_str()`   | Meaning                                        |
| --------- | ------------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `Pending`  | `"pending"`  | No data yet (idle, first load, paused await)    |
| `Error`    | `"error"`    | Last fetch failed and no data is available      |
| `Success`  | `"success"`  | Data is available                               |

### `FetchStatus` — is something running?

| Variant    | `as_str()`    | Meaning                                  |
| ---------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `Idle`      | `"idle"`      | Not fetching                             |
| `Fetching`  | `"fetching"`  | A fetch is in flight                     |
| `Paused`    | `"paused"`    | A fetch wants to run but is offline-paused |

### `MutationStatus`

`Idle` (`"idle"`), `Pending` (`"pending"`), `Success` (`"success"`), `Error` (`"error"`) — documented fully on the [mutation reference](/reference/mutations/).

### `FetchDirection`

`Forward` (pages append) and `Backward` (pages prepend) — the infinite-query pagination direction.

## Example: exhaustive rendering

<Code lang="rust" code={`use rs_query::{QueryState, QueryStatus, FetchStatus};

fn label(state: &QueryState<Vec<String>>) -> String {
    match (state.status(), state.fetch_status()) {
                    (QueryStatus::Success, FetchStatus::Fetching) => "refreshing".into(),
                    (QueryStatus::Success, FetchStatus::Idle) => "fresh".into(),
                    (QueryStatus::Pending, FetchStatus::Paused) => "waiting for network".into(),
                    (status, fetch) => format!("{:?}/{:?}", status, fetch),
    }
}`} />

## Next steps

<LinkCard title="Reference: QueryOptions" href="/reference/query-options/" description="The full option surface with defaults." />
<LinkCard title="Explanation: The caching model" href="/explanation/caching-model/" description="Why the state machine looks like this." />

# Runtime, Network, and Managers

URL: /reference/runtime-and-network/
Type: reference

rs-query runs nowhere in particular by design: spawning, timers, and signals cross a runtime seam. This page documents the seam, the network layer, and the three managers (notify, timeout, focus).

## `QueryRuntime` — the seam

| Item                             | Description                                                    |
| -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `QueryRuntime`                   | Object-safe trait: task spawning, timers, cancellation handles |
| `PoolRuntime`                    | Default: quoin's shared worker pool + portable timers          |
| `ExecutorRuntime::new(executor)` | Run on any framework executor you supply                       |
| `SpawnedTask<T>`                 | Awaitable task handle — dropping it aborts cooperatively       |
| `SpawnHandle`                    | Lower-level spawn handle (abort + join)                        |
| `BoxFuture`                      | Boxed future type used across the seam                         |

Choose a runtime once, at client construction: `QueryClient::new()` uses `PoolRuntime`, `QueryClient::with_context(&cx)` uses the framework's executor, `QueryClient::with_runtime(arc)` injects your own — the seam deterministic tests use with quoin-testkit's paused-time executor.

On `wasm32`, the pool and GC loop run their futures on the browser main thread via `spawn_local`; the OS-thread pool would panic there.

## `NetworkMode` and helpers

| Variant            | Fetch may start offline | Retries continue offline |
| ------------------ | ----------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `Online` (default) | No                      | No                       |
| `Always`           | Yes                     | Yes                      |
| `OfflineFirst`     | Yes (first attempt)     | No — retries pause       |

| Helper                            | Description                                         |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `can_fetch(mode, online) -> bool` | Whether a fetch may _start_ under this connectivity |
| `can_retry(mode, online) -> bool` | Whether a retry may _continue_                      |

## `OnlineManager`

| Member                 | Description                                           |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `OnlineManager::new()` | Starts online                                         |
| `.set_online(bool)`    | Feed platform connectivity truth; drives pause/resume |
| watch-based signals    | Runtime-free `watch` cell publishes the state         |

The client's copy lives at `client.online_manager()`; `client.handle_reconnect()` runs the reconnect sequence on top of it.

## The three managers

### `NotifyManager`

Collapses notification bursts: nested batches coalesce so one cache write storm produces one signal flush. Every cache notification passes through it.

### `TimeoutManager` and `SleepProvider`

All sleeping goes through an injectable timer source:

| Item                 | Description                                         |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `TimeoutManager`     | Schedules retries, GC sweeps, and refetch intervals |
| `SleepProvider`      | Trait for timer sources                             |
| `QuoinSleepProvider` | Runtime-free default — portable timers, no tokio    |

Swap the provider for deterministic tests: quoin-testkit's paused-time executor advances virtual clocks, so retry backoffs run instantly in CI.

### `FocusManager`

Tracks application focus events that drive `refetch_on_window_focus`. Like `OnlineManager`, your platform adapter feeds it; the crate never touches OS APIs.

## Example: a deterministic test client

<Code lang="rust" code={`use std::sync::Arc;
use rs_query::{ExecutorRuntime, QueryClient};

let client = QueryClient::with_runtime(Arc::new(ExecutorRuntime::new(
quoin_testkit::LocalExecutor::global(),
)));`} />

Inside a `#[tokio::test]` with `start_paused = true`, every internal sleep is virtual-time controlled.

# Utilities

URL: /reference/utilities/
Type: reference

The utilities round out the API surface: `streamed_query` for stream-producing fetches, `Updater` for value-or-function writes, and the `devtools` module for headless inspection.

## `streamed_query` and config

| Item                                | Description                                                  |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `streamed_query(closure)`            | Wrap a `Stream<Item = Result<T, E>>` producer for use as a fetch closure |
| `StreamedQueryConfig<T>`              | Accumulator configuration                                    |
| `.refetch_mode(RefetchMode)`          | What happens to cached data when a refetch starts            |
| `.reducer(f)`                         | Fold each streamed item into the accumulator (default: push)  |
| `.initial_value(value)`               | Seed for the accumulator                                     |

| `RefetchMode` | Refetch behavior                                        |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Replace`      | Clear cached data when the refetch starts (default)      |
| `Append`       | Keep old data; append new items after it                 |
| `Reset`        | Reset to `initial_value` when the refetch starts         |

## `Updater<T>` and functional updates

`Updater<T>` accepts either a value or a function of the previous value — the port of TanStack's value-or-function update style:

<Code lang="rust" code={`use rs_query::{Updater, functional_update};

// Value form:
let next = Updater::Value(42);
// Functional form:
let next = Updater::Function(|prev: i64| prev + 1);

// Apply it against a current value:
let applied = functional_update(next, 40); // 41`} />

`set_query_data` accepts an `Updater`, so optimistic patches can derive from the current cached data without reading it first.

## Devtools types (feature `devtools`)

| Item                              | Description                                            |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `DevtoolsState::new(client)`       | Recorder with default timeline capacity                |
| `::with_capacity(client, usize)`   | Explicit capacity                                      |
| `.record_from_client()` / `.stop_recording()` | Subscribe and collect / stop                |
| `.is_recording() -> bool`          | Recorder state                                         |
| `.cache_rows() -> Vec<CacheRow>`    | One row per cached query                               |
| `.timeline() -> Vec<TimelineEvent>` | Timestamped transitions (filtered)                     |
| `.timeline_len() -> usize` / `.clear_timeline()` | Size / reset                              |
| `.set_filter(TimelineFilter)` / `.filter()` | Narrow by kind, key prefix, text search        |
| `.refetch(cache_key)` / `.invalidate(cache_key)` / `.remove(cache_key)` | Cache actions    |
| `CacheRow`                         | Key, status, fetch status, timestamps, staleness       |
| `TimelineEvent` / `TimelineKind`    | One transition; its category                           |
| `TimelineFilter`                    | `.kind(...)`, `.key_prefix(...)`, `.search(...)`       |
| `row_fetch_status(in_flight)`       | Derive a `FetchStatus` from the in-flight flag         |

## Example: value-or-function write

<Code lang="rust" code={`use rs_query::{QueryOptions, QueryKey, Updater};

client.set_query_data::<i64>(
    &QueryKey::new("counter"),
    Updater::Function(|current| current + 1),
    QueryOptions::default(),
);`} />

<LinkCard title="Guide: Headless devtools" href="/guides/devtools/" description="Wire the recorder into your app." />

# Your First Query

URL: /tutorials/first-query/
Type: tutorial

In this tutorial you build the smallest useful rs-query program: a `QueryClient`, one `Query` with a `QueryKey`, and a single awaited fetch. You then invalidate the key and watch the cache respond. This is the golden path that every rs-query application — headless or framework-bound — builds on.

<Aside type="note">
You need a working Rust toolchain (stable, edition 2024) and the [quoin](https://github.com/elcoosp/quoin) repository checked out as a sibling directory, because rs-query depends on it by path. See [Installation](/guides/install/) if you have not set this up yet.
</Aside>

## 1. Create the project

Create a binary crate next to your `rs-query` and `quoin` checkouts:

<Code lang="bash" code={`cargo new query-demo
cd query-demo`} />

Point `Cargo.toml` at the local checkouts. The path layout matters: `quoin` resolves as `../quoin/quoin-core` from a sibling directory.

<Code lang="toml" code={`[dependencies]
rs-query = { path = "../rs-query" }
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["rt-multi-thread", "macros"] }`} />

`rs-query` itself does not need tokio — it runs on quoin's shared worker pool by default. The demo uses tokio only for its own `main`.

## 2. Create a `QueryClient`

The client owns the cache, the deduplication table, and the runtime. It is cheap to clone, and every clone shares the same cache.

<Code lang="rust" code={`use rs_query::QueryClient;

fn main() {
    let client = QueryClient::new();
    println!("client ready");
}`} />

Hold the client in your application state for the lifetime of the program.

## 3. Define a query

A `Query` pairs a `QueryKey` with an async fetch closure that returns `Result<T, E>`. Keys are hierarchical: `QueryKey::new("users")` creates the `"users"` segment, and `.with("id", 42)` appends a labelled segment.

<Code lang="rust" code={`use std::time::Duration;
use rs_query::{Query, QueryClient, QueryKey};

let client = QueryClient::new();
let key = QueryKey::new("users").with("id", 42);

let query = Query::new(key.clone(), || async {
    Ok(vec!["Ada", "Alan"])
})
.stale_time(Duration::from_secs(30));`} />

The `stale_time(30 s)` line tells the cache that the data stays fresh for thirty seconds after a successful fetch.

## 4. Run it with `spawn_query`

`spawn_query` submits the fetch to the client's runtime and returns a `SpawnedTask` — an awaitable handle you can also abort by dropping it.

<Code lang="rust" code={`use rs_query::spawn_query;

let handle = spawn_query(&client, &query);
let state = handle.await;

assert!(state.is_success());
println!("data: {:?}", state.data());`} />

Run the demo:

<Code lang="bash" code={`cargo run`} />

You should see the fetched names printed from cache.

<Aside type="tip">
Dropping a `SpawnedTask` aborts the fetch cooperatively through a `CancellationToken`. This is the mechanism behind cancel-on-unmount in framework apps.
</Aside>

## 5. Read the state machine

`state` is a `QueryState<Vec<&str>>` — an enum with one variant per cache situation:

<Code lang="text" code={`Idle → Loading → Success(T)
           → Error { error, stale_data }
Success(T) → Stale(T) → Refetching(T) → Success(T)`} />

After the awaited call in step 4 you hold `Success`. Call `state.is_stale()` after `stale_time` has elapsed to see the transition to `Stale`.

## 6. Invalidate the key

Mark the `"users"` prefix stale, refetching only the queries that currently have an active observer — the TanStack default:

<Code lang="rust" code={`use rs_query::{InvalidateQueryFilters, QueryFilters, RefetchType};

client.invalidate_queries_filtered(
    InvalidateQueryFilters::new()
                    .filters(QueryFilters::with_key(QueryKey::new("users")))
                    .refetch_type(RefetchType::Active),
);`} />

Every query whose key starts with the `"users"` segment is now stale, and active ones refetch immediately.

## What you built

A client, a keyed query, a spawned fetch, and filtered invalidation — the four moves that repeat in every rs-query application. From here, wire the same client into a UI framework, or keep going headless with imperative fetching.

## Next steps

<LinkCard title="Tutorial: Queries in a quoin app" href="/tutorials/quoin-app/" description="Observe the same query from a framework view with use_query." />
<LinkCard title="Guide: Running queries" href="/guides/queries/" description="Imperative fetching, prefetching, and cancellation patterns." />

# Queries in a Quoin App

URL: /tutorials/quoin-app/
Type: tutorial

In this tutorial you take the headless query from the [first tutorial](/tutorials/first-query/) and observe it from inside a quoin application. The bindings are generic over any `quoin_core::ReactiveContext`, so the code below is identical on gpui, leptos, dioxus, xilem, and floem — only the surrounding view syntax differs. Every binding returns your framework's **own** signal type.

<Aside type="note">
Prerequisites: a quoin application skeleton with a `ReactiveContext` available (usually `cx`), and the [installation](/guides/install/) from the first tutorial.
</Aside>

## 1. Build the client from the framework context

Construct the client with `QueryClient::with_context(&cx)` so fetches and timers ride the framework's own executor instead of the default worker pool:

<Code lang="rust" code={`use rs_query::QueryClient;

// Inside your app setup:
let client = QueryClient::with_context(&cx);`} />

Store the client in your application state. Like `QueryClient::new()`, it is cheap to clone and shares one cache across clones.

## 2. Observe a query from a view

Inside a component, call `use_query` with the context, the client, and the query. The binding pumps cache updates into a framework signal and stays in sync through lag-tolerant cache pumps:

<Code lang="rust" code={`use rs_query::use_query;

// Inside a component, where cx is the framework's ReactiveContext:
let todo = use_query(&cx, &client, &query);

// todo.state is the framework's own signal: read it from your view.
let state = todo.state.get(); // QueryState<Todo>`} />

Dropping the binding cancels its pump and aborts the in-flight fetch — cancel-on-unmount is the default behavior, not an opt-in.

## 3. Render the state

`QueryState<T>` has a variant for every cache situation, so `match` covers rendering exhaustively:

<Code lang="rust" code={`match state {
    rs_query::QueryState::Idle | rs_query::QueryState::Loading => render_spinner(),
    rs_query::QueryState::LoadingWithPlaceholder(data)
    | rs_query::QueryState::Success(data)
    | rs_query::QueryState::Stale(data)
    | rs_query::QueryState::Refetching(data) => render_todo(data),
    rs_query::QueryState::Error { error, stale_data } => match stale_data {
                    Some(data) => render_todo_with_banner(data, error),
                    None => render_error(error),
    },
}`} />

<Aside type="tip">
You rarely write this match by hand. The [QueryObserver](/reference/observers/) result flags — `is_placeholder_data`, `is_refetch_error`, `is_paused` — exist to turn these branches into compact boolean logic.
</Aside>

## 4. Trigger a refetch from the view

The binding exposes `refetch` and `abort_fetch` for user-driven actions:

<Code lang="rust" code={`todo.refetch();     // re-run the query now
todo.abort_fetch(); // cancel the in-flight fetch`} />

## 5. Mutate and invalidate

Wire a save button to a mutation with `use_mutation`, and invalidate the list key on success. The mutation lifecycle runs cache-level and options-level hooks in TanStack order (see [Mutations and optimistic updates](/guides/mutations/)):

<Code lang="rust" code={`use rs_query::{Mutation, MutateOptions};

let save = use_mutation(&cx, &client, &save_mutation);

// On button click:
save.mutate(patch, MutateOptions::new().on_success(|_client, _data| {
    // the mutation's own invalidates_key already refetched active queries
}));`} />

The signal updates again when the invalidated query refetches — no manual wiring between mutation and view.

## 6. Gate rendering during hydration

If the client restores persisted state at startup, hold the `is_restoring` flag until the restore finishes. Bindings respect the gate and hold `fetchStatus` at `idle` while it is set:

<Code lang="rust" code={`client.set_is_restoring(true);
// ... restore ...
client.set_is_restoring(false);`} />

## What you built

A framework-bound query with cancel-on-unmount, exhaustive state rendering, user-driven refetch, mutation-driven invalidation, and a hydration gate — the full reactive loop, without a single framework-specific import in the query layer.
